_about: Round-3 end-to-end extraction eval (2026-06-04). Fresh, held-out content (not in gold.json). Each memory probes a specific item from the residual fix backlog plus general quality. Added in array order via HTTP MCP so supersession ordering is deterministic. gold = the evaluator's expectation; graders verify independently against the taxonomy contract.

memories.content: Redis is our primary cache layer; every API node reads session state from it on each request.
memories.probe: Supersession TARGET setup (must stay active after m02). redis typed database via override -> technologies populated.

memories.content: We chose Valkey over Redis for the cache to avoid the new licensing terms.
memories.probe: BACKLOG-7 (HIGH): 'chose X over Y' is SELECTION -> IMPROVES_ON, NOT REPLACES. CRITICAL: must NOT supersede m01 (redis stays active). Valkey is uncurated -> watch its type.

memories.content: Last sprint we migrated the job queue from RabbitMQ to NATS to cut operational overhead.
memories.probe: REAL migration language ('migrated from X to Y') -> REPLACES fires correctly (isolated; no pre-existing rabbitmq target so no flip). Contrast with m02 selection.

memories.content: The export job crashes whenever the S3 bucket is unreachable, because it buffers the entire dataset in memory before flushing.
memories.probe: BACKLOG-4 (HIGH): hard dependency ('crashes whenever unreachable') -> DEPENDS_ON not USES. Causal core (in-memory buffering -> crash) is the known-unrepresented case; note whether captured.

memories.content: After the February outage, Priya Nair's load test showed the API gateway dropping requests above 5,000 RPS.
memories.probe: BACKLOG-3 (HIGH): temporal 'after the February outage' must NOT fabricate a CAUSES edge; authorship must NOT fabricate 'priya nair MENTIONS api gateway'. '5,000 RPS' is a literal, not an entity.

memories.content: Set producer.linger.ms to 50 and point the broker at 10.2.0.14:9092 before load testing.
memories.probe: BACKLOG-5/6 (MEDIUM): dotted config-key stems ('producer','linger') must NOT become concept entities; IP '10.2.0.14', port '9092', value '50' must be blocklisted; NO bogus DEPLOYED_ON to the IP.

memories.content: On 2026-05-20, Marcus Lee shipped the auth module written in Go; it follows RFC 7519 for signing tokens.
memories.probe: BACKLOG-LOW: 'follows RFC 7519' -> IMPLEMENTS/IS_A not CITES; short language 'Go' survives the <3-char filter; HAPPENED_ON(date) + AUTHORED_BY both extracted.

memories.content: I always run the formatter with --write before opening a pull request, never by hand.
memories.probe: Value-literal restraint: '--write' is a flag, not an entity. Preference classification. 'never by hand' must not spawn odd edges.

memories.content: The recommendation engine runs on Kubernetes and pulls feature vectors from Feast at inference time.
memories.probe: 'runs on' -> DEPLOYED_ON vs 'pulls from' -> USES. kubernetes typed tool via override; feast uncurated (watch type).

memories.content: The Raft paper by Diego Ongaro and John Ousterhout is our canonical reference for the consensus layer.
memories.probe: Author FAN-OUT over 2 people ('by A and B' -> 2 AUTHORED_BY edges). reference classification.

memories.content: The billing service does not use the legacy ledger; all writes now go through the event bus.
memories.probe: NEGATION (rule 10 + regex): 'does not use the legacy ledger' must NOT yield billing->legacy ledger USES/DEPENDS_ON. The positive 'event bus' edge must survive.

memories.content: The web dashboard, the mobile app, and the partner API all authenticate through Keycloak.
memories.probe: BACKLOG-1 (HIGH, headline): coordinated-subject FAN-OUT. 'A, B and C all use X' must yield 3 edges, one per subject. Also: web dashboard/mobile app are named app surfaces -> artifact, must be extracted despite common head nouns.
